cohort: Pregnancies managed at Central Hospital Warri, Delta State, Nigeria between 2014-2017 (n=14,067), with a focus on teenage pregnancies (n=399)
finding: Teenage pregnancy was associated with a higher risk of complications, particularly among younger teenagers, including increased rates of iron deficiency anemia, low birth weight infants, and perineal laceration.
mod_finding: Younger teenagers were more likely to have a cesarean delivery compared to older teenagers.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was an outcome, but specific weight criteria were not mentioned.
